                    ### Question
                    An otherwise healthy 27-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with dark urine and left flank pain. He has had a fever, sore throat, and malaise for the last 2 days. Vital signs reveal a temperature of 38.1°C (100.5°F), blood pressure of 120/82 mm Hg, and a pulse of 95/min. His family history is noncontributory. Physical examination reveals enlarged tonsils with tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy. Urinalysis shows pink urine with 20–25 red cells/high power field and 2+ protein. This patient’s condition is most likely due to which of the following?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Inherited abnormalities in type IV collagen
opb. Autoantibodies against alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen
opc. C3 nephritic factor
opd. Immune complex deposition
ope. Diffuse mesangial IgA deposition

The patient's presentation with dark urine, flank pain, fever, sore throat, and malaise, along with urinalysis findings of red cells and protein, is most likely due to a post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis. This is supported by the chain: Streptococcal infection -> Activation of alternative complement pathway -> C3 nephritic factor production -> Glomerulonephritis. The evidence paths indicating (Antigen-Antibody Complex)-CAUSES->(Symptoms)-CAUSES->(Glomerulonephritis) and (Antigen-Antibody Complex)-CAUSES->(Kidney Diseases)-CAUSES->(Glomerulonephritis) align with the consensus that immune complex deposition in the kidney leads to glomerulonephritis in this context.
